topics.growth: Natural leaves can decay when no longer connected to nearby logs. Leaves you place yourself do not decay. Use a matching sapling to grow a new tree; bone meal does not turn a leaf block into a tree.

topics.location: Get saplings by breaking or letting leaves decay from matching trees in forests and plains.
topics.growth: Plant the sapling on suitable dirt-like soil with enough light and clear space above it. Bone meal can speed up growth.

topics.location: Get saplings by breaking or letting leaves decay from matching trees in dappled forests.
topics.growth: Plant the sapling on suitable dirt-like soil with enough light and clear space above it. Bone meal can speed up growth.

topics.mining: Use shears or a Silk Touch tool to collect azalea leaves. Otherwise they may drop the corresponding azalea shrub. Fortune improves the shrub-drop chance.
topics.location: Find azalea leaves on azalea trees above lush caves. Flowering leaves and ordinary azalea leaves are different decorative variants.
topics.growth: Grow an azalea or flowering azalea with bone meal to make an azalea tree. Leaf blocks themselves are not saplings.

topics.mining: Azaleas drop themselves when broken by hand or with any tool. Shears are unnecessary.
topics.location: Find azaleas in lush caves, or grow vegetation by using bone meal on moss blocks.
topics.growth: Place an azalea on suitable soil and use bone meal to grow an azalea tree, leaving enough room above. Flowering and nonflowering azaleas can both grow into trees.

topics.mining: Use shears or a Silk Touch tool to collect mangrove leaves. Grow and collect propagules beneath the leaves to plant more mangrove trees; do not expect an ordinary mangrove sapling drop.
topics.location: Find mangrove leaves on mangrove trees in mangrove swamps.
topics.growth: Use bone meal on mangrove leaves with empty space underneath to start a hanging propagule. Use more bone meal on the propagule to mature it.

topics.mining: Collect hanging propagules only when fully mature. Immature hanging propagules drop nothing. A planted propagule drops itself when broken.
topics.location: Look beneath mangrove leaves in mangrove swamps for hanging propagules.
topics.growth: Let a hanging propagule mature before collecting it. Plant it on suitable soil, including underwater, with enough room for a mangrove tree. Bone meal can speed its growth.

topics.mining: Harvest by breaking the mature crop by hand or with a tool. Mature wheat gives 1 wheat plus a variable number of seeds. Fortune increases seed yield, not the wheat count. Replant after harvesting.
topics.location: Look for this crop in village farms. You can also get wheat seeds by breaking grass.
topics.growth: Plant wheat seeds on farmland. Light level 9 or above supports normal growth. Nearby water keeps farmland hydrated; bone meal speeds up the crop. Protect farmland from trampling.

topics.mining: Harvest by breaking the mature crop by hand or with a tool. A mature carrot crop normally gives 2–5 carrots. Fortune can increase the yield. Replant after harvesting.
topics.location: Look for this crop in village farms. Keep some of the planting material for your own farm.
topics.growth: Plant carrots on farmland. Light level 9 or above supports normal growth. Nearby water keeps farmland hydrated; bone meal speeds up the crop. Protect farmland from trampling.

topics.mining: Harvest by breaking the mature crop by hand or with a tool. A mature potato crop normally gives 2–5 potatoes and has a small chance of an extra poisonous potato. Fortune can increase ordinary potato yield. Replant after harvesting.
topics.location: Look for this crop in village farms. Keep some of the planting material for your own farm.
topics.growth: Plant potatoes on farmland. Light level 9 or above supports normal growth. Nearby water keeps farmland hydrated; bone meal speeds up the crop. Protect farmland from trampling.

topics.mining: Harvest by breaking the mature crop by hand or with a tool. A mature beetroot crop gives beetroot and seeds. Fortune improves the seed yield, not the beetroot count. Replant after harvesting.
topics.location: Look for this crop in village farms. Keep some of the planting material for your own farm.
topics.growth: Plant beetroot seeds on farmland. Light level 9 or above supports normal growth. Nearby water keeps farmland hydrated; bone meal speeds up the crop. Protect farmland from trampling.

topics.mining: Breaking farmland drops dirt, not a farmland item; a shovel is fastest. Silk Touch does not collect farmland intact.
topics.location: Use a hoe on dirt or grass blocks to make farmland. Village farms also contain it.
topics.growth: Farmland supports crops. Water up to 4 blocks away horizontally, at the same level or one block above, can hydrate it. Dry empty farmland can turn back into dirt; trampling can also destroy it.
topics.water: Water nearby hydrates farmland. Putting water directly into its block space destroys the farmland rather than waterlogging it.

topics.mining: Mature Nether wart yields 2–4 Nether wart; Fortune can increase the yield. Immature plants give 1. Harvest by hand or with any tool and replant some.
topics.location: Look in Nether fortresses and some housing-unit bastion remnants for Nether wart gardens.
topics.growth: Plant Nether wart on soul sand, not soul soil. It can grow in any dimension and does not need water or light. Bone meal does not speed it up.

topics.mining: Break the upper sugar cane blocks and leave the bottom one to regrow. The blocks drop sugar cane; no special tool is required. Fortune does not multiply the yield.
topics.location: Find sugar cane beside water on riverbanks and shorelines.
topics.growth: Plant sugar cane on suitable soil or sand directly beside water. It naturally grows upward to 3 blocks. Bone meal speeds its growth.
topics.water: Sugar cane needs water beside the supporting soil, not poured over the cane itself. Removing nearby water can uproot it.

topics.mining: Cactus can be broken by hand and drops itself. Break upper segments and leave the base to regrow. Keep dropped items away from cactus, which can destroy them.
topics.location: Find cactus in deserts and badlands.
topics.growth: Plant cactus on sand or red sand with the sides clear of obstructing blocks. It grows upward naturally. It does not need water; bone meal does not speed its growth.

topics.mining: Bamboo drops bamboo when broken. A sword breaks stalks instantly. Leave the bottom segment to regrow; breaking a lower segment breaks the bamboo above it too.
topics.location: Find bamboo in jungles, particularly bamboo jungles.
topics.growth: Plant bamboo on suitable soil and leave space above it. It grows tall naturally; bone meal speeds growth. It does not need adjacent water.

topics.mining: A mature cocoa pod drops 3 cocoa beans. An axe is fastest. Fortune does not increase the yield. Replant cocoa beans on a suitable jungle wood surface.
topics.location: Look for cocoa pods attached to jungle trees in jungles.
topics.growth: Plant cocoa beans on the side of jungle logs or jungle wood, including stripped versions. The wood need not be part of a living tree. Bone meal speeds up pod growth; water is unnecessary.

topics.mining: Use a grown sweet berry bush to pick berries without destroying it. A fully grown bush gives 2–3 berries and returns to an earlier growth stage. Breaking a grown bush can also yield berries.
topics.location: Look for sweet berry bushes in taiga and snowy taiga biomes.
topics.growth: Plant sweet berries on suitable soil. Bone meal speeds bush growth. Grown bushes slow and can hurt most mobs and players who move through them.

topics.mining: Harvest the mature crop to get a torchflower. Breaking it before maturity returns its planting material instead. A mature crop does not return extra seeds or pods.
topics.location: Have an adult sniffer dig up torchflower seeds from suitable ground, then plant them to grow this crop.
topics.growth: Plant torchflower seeds on farmland with enough light. Bone meal speeds growth. Harvest the mature plant and obtain more planting material from sniffers.

topics.mining: Harvest the mature crop to get a pitcher plant. Breaking it before maturity returns its planting material instead. A mature crop does not return extra seeds or pods.
topics.location: Have an adult sniffer dig up pitcher pods from suitable ground, then plant them to grow this crop.
topics.growth: Plant pitcher pods on farmland with enough light. Bone meal speeds growth. Harvest the mature plant and obtain more planting material from sniffers.

topics.mining: Break kelp by hand or with any tool. Each broken segment drops kelp; breaking a lower segment also breaks those above it. Leave the base to regrow.
topics.location: Look oceans except warm and frozen oceans.
topics.growth: Plant kelp underwater on a suitable solid surface with water above it. Bone meal can extend it upward.
topics.water: This aquatic plant needs water to survive. Do not drain its growing space.

topics.mining: Use shears to collect seagrass. Other ordinary tools, including Silk Touch tools without shears, do not collect it. Tall seagrass gives 2 seagrass items.
topics.location: Look underwater in rivers and many ocean biomes.
topics.growth: Use bone meal underwater on suitable blocks to grow seagrass. It must stay in water.
topics.water: This aquatic plant needs water to survive. Do not drain its growing space.

topics.mining: Use shears to collect ordinary vines. Silk Touch on another tool does not collect them. Breaking their support can destroy hanging vines without collecting them.
topics.location: Find vines in jungles and swamps, hanging from trees and other surfaces.
topics.growth: Place vines against a suitable support. They spread over nearby surfaces and hang downward. Bone meal does not speed up ordinary vines.

topics.mining: Use shears or Silk Touch to guarantee a vine drop from the segment you break. Fortune III also guarantees its drop; otherwise drops are not guaranteed. Harvest from the top so unsupported segments are not wasted.
topics.location: Find these vines in warped forests in the Nether.
topics.growth: These vines grow upward. Bone meal extends the growing tip when space is available.

topics.mining: Use shears or Silk Touch to guarantee a vine drop from the segment you break. Fortune III also guarantees its drop; otherwise drops are not guaranteed. Harvest from the bottom so unsupported segments are not wasted.
topics.location: Find these vines in crimson forests in the Nether.
topics.growth: These vines grow downward. Bone meal extends the growing tip when space is available.

topics.mining: Moss drops itself by hand or with any tool; a hoe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary and Fortune does not increase the block drop.
topics.location: Find moss on the floor and ceiling of lush caves, or obtain it from some loot and wandering traders.
topics.growth: Use bone meal on moss to spread it over nearby convertible blocks with air above. This can also grow moss carpet, grass and azaleas. Not every block is convertible.

topics.mining: Moss carpet drops itself by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Find moss carpet in lush caves, grow it by bone-mealing moss blocks, or craft it from moss blocks.
topics.growth: Moss carpet is a thin decorative layer. Use bone meal on a moss block to spread moss vegetation; carpet is not the same as a moss block.

topics.mining: Break the chorus flower itself to collect it. Breaking the supporting chorus plant does not collect the flowers for you. An axe is fastest.
topics.location: Find chorus flowers at the tips of chorus plants on the outer End islands.
topics.growth: Plant a chorus flower on End stone with space around and above it. It grows a branching chorus plant. Bone meal does not speed it up.

topics.mining: Breaking chorus plant stems gives a chance of chorus fruit, not a placeable stem block. Breaking the base collapses the connected plant. Harvest flowers separately first if you want to replant.
topics.location: Find chorus plants on the outer End islands.
topics.growth: Grow a new chorus plant by placing a chorus flower on End stone. Leave room for branches. Stem blocks are not the planting item.

topics.mining: Use a Silk Touch pickaxe to collect the live coral block. A pickaxe without Silk Touch gives the dead block instead.
topics.location: Look in coral reefs in warm oceans.
topics.water: Keep live coral in contact with suitable water to prevent it from turning into dead coral. Putting dead coral back in water does not revive it.

topics.mining: Use a Silk Touch tool to collect this coral plant. Without Silk Touch it drops nothing.
topics.location: Look in coral reefs in warm oceans.
topics.water: Keep live coral in contact with suitable water to prevent it from turning into dead coral. Putting dead coral back in water does not revive it.

topics.mining: Use a Silk Touch tool to collect this coral decoration. Without Silk Touch it drops nothing. Wall-mounted fans drop their matching fan item, not a separate wall-fan item.
topics.location: Look in coral reefs in warm oceans.
topics.water: Keep live coral in contact with suitable water to prevent it from turning into dead coral. Putting dead coral back in water does not revive it.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect the dead coral block. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Look in coral reefs in warm oceans.
topics.water: Dead coral stays dead in water; it cannot be revived by adding water or bone meal.

topics.mining: Use a Silk Touch tool to collect this coral plant. Without Silk Touch it drops nothing.
topics.location: Look in coral reefs in warm oceans.
topics.water: Dead coral stays dead in water; it cannot be revived by adding water or bone meal.

topics.mining: Use a Silk Touch tool to collect this coral decoration. Without Silk Touch it drops nothing. Wall-mounted fans drop their matching fan item, not a separate wall-fan item.
topics.location: Look in coral reefs in warm oceans.
topics.water: Dead coral stays dead in water; it cannot be revived by adding water or bone meal.

topics.location: Look in many grassy Overworld biomes, including plains for this flower.
topics.growth: Place the flower on suitable dirt-like soil with enough light. Flowers are not farmland crops and do not need nearby irrigation water.

topics.mining: Use shears or a Silk Touch tool to collect hanging roots. Without either, they drop nothing.
topics.location: Look beneath rooted dirt in lush caves, or use bone meal on rooted dirt to grow hanging roots underneath.
topics.growth: Use bone meal on rooted dirt with empty space below to grow hanging roots. Using a hoe on rooted dirt also removes the roots and turns it into dirt.

topics.mining: Mangrove roots drop themselves by hand or with any tool; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Find roots around mangrove trees in mangrove swamps, or grow a mangrove propagule.
topics.water: Mangrove roots can be waterlogged, even though they fill a full block space.

topics.mining: Muddy mangrove roots drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a shovel is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Look where mangrove roots meet mud in mangrove swamps, or craft the block from mud and mangrove roots.

topics.mining: Use a berry-bearing cave vine to collect 1 glow berry without breaking it. Breaking a vine also yields 1 glow berry if it has berries, or nothing if it has none. Fortune does not increase the yield.
topics.location: Find cave vines hanging from ceilings in lush caves.
topics.growth: Place glow berries under a block to start hanging cave vines. Use bone meal on a cave vine to make it bear berries. Vines grow downward when space is clear.

topics.mining: Big dripleaf can be harvested with any tool; an axe is fastest. Breaking any part collapses the plant, dropping big dripleaf from its parts.
topics.location: Find big dripleaf in lush caves.
topics.growth: Bone meal can grow a small dripleaf into a big dripleaf and can make a big dripleaf taller. Leave space above. Its leaf temporarily tilts when stood on.

topics.mining: Use shears to collect small dripleaf. Other tools, breaking its support or piston movement drop nothing.
topics.location: Find small dripleaf in lush caves, or buy it from wandering traders.
topics.growth: Bone meal turns small dripleaf into big dripleaf. It does not multiply small dripleaves; use wandering traders for a renewable supply.

topics.mining: Pale moss drops itself by hand or with any tool; a hoe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Find pale moss patches in pale gardens.
topics.growth: Use bone meal on pale moss blocks to spread pale moss over nearby convertible blocks and grow pale moss carpet.

topics.mining: Pale moss carpet drops itself when broken by hand or with a tool.
topics.location: Find pale moss carpet on pale moss patches in pale gardens.
topics.growth: Pale moss carpet can grow decorative side coverings against neighboring solid blocks. Bone meal can grow these side coverings; it is not ordinary farmland.

topics.mining: Use shears or a Silk Touch tool to collect pale hanging moss. Otherwise it drops nothing.
topics.location: Find pale hanging moss under pale oak leaves and logs in pale gardens. Sapling-grown pale oaks do not automatically generate it.
topics.growth: Pale hanging moss does not naturally extend after placement. Use bone meal to extend it downward when there is room.

topics.mining: Fungi drop themselves when broken by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Find this fungus in crimson forests in the Nether.
topics.growth: Use bone meal on this fungus planted on crimson nylium to grow its matching huge fungus. Leave enough room. Normal planting soil and huge-fungus growth requirements are different.

topics.mining: Fungi drop themselves when broken by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Find this fungus in warped forests in the Nether.
topics.growth: Use bone meal on this fungus planted on warped nylium to grow its matching huge fungus. Leave enough room. Normal planting soil and huge-fungus growth requirements are different.

topics.mining: Nether roots drop themselves when broken by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Find crimson roots in crimson forests and warped roots in warped forests in the Nether.
topics.growth: Nether roots are decorative vegetation, not tree saplings. Bone meal on nylium grows Nether vegetation, including appropriate roots.

topics.mining: Small mushrooms drop themselves when broken by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Look in dark areas, forests, mushroom fields and parts of the Nether for mushrooms.
topics.growth: Mushrooms can spread in suitable dim conditions. On mycelium, podzol or nylium they can be planted regardless of light. Bone meal can grow a huge mushroom when substrate and space requirements are met.

topics.mining: Use Silk Touch to collect the mushroom block itself. Cap blocks broken without Silk Touch can drop mushrooms; mushroom stems do not yield mushrooms. An axe is fastest.
topics.location: Find huge mushrooms in mushroom fields and dark forests, or grow a small mushroom with bone meal under suitable conditions.
topics.growth: Huge mushroom blocks are building materials, not seeds for another huge mushroom. Use bone meal on a small red or brown mushroom to grow one.

topics.mining: Use shears to collect ferns; a large fern gives 2 fern items. Without shears they may drop wheat seeds instead. Fortune can improve the seed yield.
topics.location: Look in jungles and taiga biomes for ferns.
topics.growth: Place ferns on suitable dirt-like soil. Bone meal on a fern can grow a large fern.

topics.mining: Use shears to collect grass plants. Otherwise they may drop wheat seeds. Fortune can improve the seed yield. Tall grass gives short grass items rather than a separate tall-grass item.
topics.location: Look on grassy terrain in many Overworld biomes.
topics.growth: Use bone meal on grass blocks to generate vegetation appropriate to the biome. Bone meal on short grass can grow tall grass.

topics.mining: Lily pads drop themselves when broken by hand or with any tool. Boats can also break them.
topics.location: Find lily pads on water in swamps and mangrove swamps.
topics.growth: Lily pads are placed on water surfaces. They do not grow taller or spread by themselves, and bone meal does not multiply them.

topics.mining: A melon normally drops 3–7 melon slices. Fortune can increase the yield, capped at 9 slices. Silk Touch collects the whole melon. An axe is fastest.
topics.location: Find melons in jungles or grow them from melon seeds.
topics.growth: Plant melon seeds on farmland to grow a stem. Once mature, the stem needs an adjacent suitable empty growing space to produce a melon. Harvest the melon while leaving the stem for more fruit.

topics.mining: Pumpkins drop themselves by hand or with any tool; an axe is fastest. Use shears on a pumpkin to carve it and obtain pumpkin seeds.
topics.location: Find pumpkin patches in grassy Overworld terrain, or grow pumpkins from seeds.
topics.growth: Plant pumpkin seeds on farmland to grow a stem. Leave a suitable empty space beside the mature stem for a pumpkin to appear. Harvest the pumpkin and leave the stem for more fruit.

topics.mining: Breaking a stem can give its corresponding seeds. Harvest the fruit instead and leave the stem if you want it to keep producing.
topics.location: Plant melon seeds on farmland to obtain the stem.
topics.growth: Grow the stem on farmland with enough light and a suitable adjacent empty space for fruit. Bone meal matures the stem but does not instantly create the fruit.
